messages:
Mike: Heads-up: multiple customers reporting streaming responses abruptly cut with 'broken pipe' after a few KB, and our platform is marking those as 5xx. ticket SUP-8321. Anyone else seeing this?

Jessica: Yep saw a small bump in streaming 5xx this morning. Gateway logs show write errors: 'write: broken pipe' and some upstream EOFs. Looks correlated to rapid reconnects from a handful of mobile clients.

Sam: Can you paste a sample request_id and a minimal repro curl? Are clients using chunked Transfer-Encoding and connection reuse?

Mike: Sample curl from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' \
  -d @prompt.txt https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
```
Customer says stream sends ~2-8 KB then connection dies, client sees broken pipe.

Jessica: Gateway log snippet for request_id=abc123def:
```
[2026-03-16T15:06:02Z] request_id=abc123def method=POST path=/v1/streams/generate up_err=EOF write_err="write: broken pipe" conn_state=halfclose
```
Upstream (runtime) shows kv-cache hit then sudden peer reset.

infra-bot: Alert: upstream_reset_rate increased 4.6x in us-west-2 between 15:02-15:22 UTC (affected path /v1/streams/*). Link: https://internal/alerts/8472

Anna: Affected customers say their mobile SDK reconnect logic retries quickly on flaky LTE, so we may be seeing lots of short-lived connections. They insist this should not be billed as 5xx.

Sam: Hypothesis: client FIN or TCP RST arriving while gateway is mid-chunk leads to a race where we attribute the failure to the upstream and classify as 5xx. Need to confirm whether our EOF/pipe heuristics treat client-initiated close as gateway error.

Jessica: I instrumented the proxy: if remote FIN observed within 200ms of the last chunk, we currently mark as upstream_error for metering. That seems too aggressive for flaky clients.

Mike: Quick repro I ran locally: start a chunked server that streams a few chunks, then send FIN from client after 100ms:
```
# server: node stream_server.js (sends 3 chunks, sleeps)
# client: nc host port; send headers; then send FIN after 120ms using socat + -T
```
I could reproduce broken-pipe the same way.

Sam: Proposed immediate mitigations: (1) change metrics/classification so a client-close within X ms of last chunk is considered client-abort (not 5xx) for billing/alerts; (2) add a short ingress grace window to accept in-flight chunk trailer completion before escalating.

Jessica: Agreed. Also add a debug flag to keep full tcp traces for a day for impacted request_ids. I'll push a small logging flip.

Sam: I'll open an incident and route to eng-runtime for a quick config rollback on classification. tagging @Jessica @Mike. Incident: INC-2026-201.

Mike: FYI customer-facing note drafted in SUP-8321: explain transient mobile reconnects, offer to validate client retry backoff and SDK patch.

Anna: Customer asks for credits if they were billed for these. We should pause billing changes until we confirm scope.

Jessica: Count estimate: ~1200 streams in the window, ~8 customers. Will follow up after eng-runtime confirms classification change.

Sam: Action items: Jessica -> flip debug logging and share sample traces; Eng-runtime -> adjust classification flag; Support -> hold credits pending scope. I'll update INC-2026-201.

Mike: thanks, looping in eng-runtime on pager. :thumbsup:
